title: Atezolizumab in early triple-negative breast cancer
summary: Atezolizumab increased pCR from 57.0% to 63.3% (+6.3 percentage points), but 4-year EFS was 85.2% vs 81.9% (+3.3 points), HR 0.80 (95% CI 0.62–1.03; P=.083).
criticalReview: In a potentially curable breast cancer, is a 6.3% increase in pCR, or a 3.3% absolute improvement in 4-year EFS that did not reach statistical significance, worth more than doubling treatment discontinuation due to adverse events, from 10.6% to 21.2%? Immune-related adverse events occurred in 27.6% vs 11.4%. The real question is not whether atezolizumab improves pCR, but whether the magnitude of long-term benefit is large enough to justify the additional toxicity, treatment discontinuation and financial burden in a curable disease.

title: Salvage radiotherapy with or without long-term antiandrogen therapy after prostatectomy
journal: International Journal of Radiation Oncology, Biology, Physics
population: 760 eligible men after prostatectomy with pT3N0 or pT2N0 with positive margins and PSA 0.2–4.0 ng/mL
summary: At a median follow-up of 18.9 years, 18-year overall survival was 53% with salvage prostate-bed RT plus 24 months of bicalutamide versus 43% with RT plus placebo, an absolute improvement of 9.8 percentage points (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.67–1.00). The 18-year incidence of metastatic prostate cancer was 22% vs 31%, an absolute reduction of 9 points.
criticalReview: This is unusually mature evidence for the salvage setting: adding 24 months of bicalutamide to prostate-bed RT produced a clinically meaningful 9.8-point improvement in 18-year overall survival and a 9-point reduction in metastatic disease. The trade-off is substantial androgen-related toxicity, particularly gynecomastia, which occurred in 69.7% versus 10.9% in the original report. The key contemporary question is therefore not whether long-term hormonal intensification works, but which patients still need prolonged therapy in the era of early salvage RT, PSMA imaging and shorter-duration ADT strategies.

title: Perioperative apalutamide in high-risk localized prostate cancer
population: 2109 men with newly diagnosed high-risk localized or locally advanced prostate cancer undergoing radical prostatectomy with pelvic lymph-node dissection
summary: At median follow-up of 61.7 months, perioperative ADT plus apalutamide increased 5-year metastasis-free survival from 73.5% to 78.2%, an absolute improvement of 4.7 percentage points (HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.67–0.96; P=.02). Pathological complete response or minimal residual disease was 8.9% vs 1.0% (OR 10.17, 95% CI 5.27–19.64).
criticalReview: PROTEUS provides randomized phase III evidence that six cycles of perioperative apalutamide added to ADT before and after prostatectomy improves metastasis-free survival in high-risk localized or locally advanced prostate cancer. The absolute 5-year metastasis-free survival gain was 4.7 percentage points, while grade 3–4 adverse events increased from 31.0% to 39.6%. The key clinical question is whether this modest absolute metastasis-free survival gain justifies substantially greater treatment intensity and toxicity for all patients meeting the high-risk definition.

title: Atezolizumab plus SBRT versus SBRT alone in high-risk early-stage NSCLC
population: 402 eligible patients with T1–T3N0M0 NSCLC ≤7 cm, medically inoperable or declining surgery, with at least one prespecified high-risk feature
summary: At median follow-up of 24.8 months, overall survival was not improved with atezolizumab plus SBRT: HR 1.04 (95% CI 0.69–1.58; one-sided P=.58), with 2-year OS 82% in both groups. Grade ≥3 adverse events were 12% versus 3%, an absolute increase of 9 percentage points, and two grade 5 respiratory events occurred with atezolizumab. The trial closed early for futility.
criticalReview: S1914 is a negative phase III trial and directly challenges the assumption that the PACIFIC/ADRIATIC consolidation paradigm can simply be transplanted onto SBRT. SBRT already achieves very high local control, so the incremental opportunity for systemic therapy depends on the amount of clinically meaningful micrometastatic disease remaining after local ablation. The S1914 population was also predominantly elderly and medically inoperable, with greater competing mortality and treatment vulnerability than the fitter populations enrolled in PACIFIC and ADRIATIC. Importantly, S1914 gave atezolizumab before, during and after SBRT, so the result cannot be explained simply by starting immunotherapy too late. The more plausible explanation is that SBRT does not recreate the immunological and systemic-disease context of definitive chemoradiotherapy: chemotherapy contributes immunogenic cell death, antigen release and inflammatory signalling, while definitive CRT treats a larger regional tumour burden and identifies a population that has demonstrated disease control after intensive treatment. PACIFIC and ADRIATIC therefore select patients with a higher residual systemic-risk state in whom prolonged checkpoint blockade has a larger absolute opportunity to prevent relapse. S1914 should not be read as evidence that radiation-immunotherapy synergy is biologically impossible; rather, it shows that routine atezolizumab with SBRT does not improve survival and adds meaningful toxicity. Biomarker selection, driver-mutation exclusion, residual systemic-risk enrichment and optimal sequencing remain important questions for future SBRT-immunotherapy trials.

title: Perioperative durvalumab plus FLOT for resectable gastric and gastro-oesophageal junction adenocarcinoma
population: 948 adults with previously untreated, resectable stage II–IVa gastric or GEJ adenocarcinoma
summary: At 36 months, overall survival was 68.6% with durvalumab plus FLOT versus 61.9% with placebo plus FLOT, an absolute improvement of 6.7 percentage points (HR 0.78, 95% CI 0.63–0.96; P=.021). Two-year EFS was 67.4% versus 58.5%, an absolute improvement of 8.9 points (HR 0.71, 95% CI 0.58–0.86; P<.001).
criticalReview: MATTERHORN provides randomized phase III evidence that adding perioperative durvalumab to FLOT improves both EFS and OS. The absolute OS gain at 3 years is 6.7 percentage points, while the pCR gain is 12 points. The trade-off is additional immunotherapy and immune-related toxicity within an already intensive perioperative regimen. The trial was not designed to isolate the contribution of each treatment phase.

title: Tambotatug pelitecan versus topotecan in relapsed small-cell lung cancer
population: 451 patients with relapsed SCLC after one prior platinum-based regimen
summary: Tambotatug pelitecan improved median overall survival to 13.3 months versus 9.4 months with topotecan (HR 0.46, 95% CI 0.35–0.62; P<.001) and median PFS to 7.4 versus 2.8 months (HR 0.29, 95% CI 0.23–0.37; P<.001). Objective response rate was 59.1% versus 9.7%, an absolute increase of 49.4 percentage points.
criticalReview: TAISHAN-302 is a randomized phase III trial showing a large improvement in OS, PFS and response with the B7-H3-directed ADC tambotatug pelitecan compared with topotecan after platinum therapy. The magnitude of response and PFS improvement is substantial, but interpretation should consider the Chinese study population, the open-label design and the maturity of the interim OS analysis. Tam-Peli is a targeted cytotoxic ADC: the antibody binds B7-H3, the complex is internalized, and a camptothecin-derived topoisomerase-I inhibitor payload is released. This produces replication-associated DNA damage and apoptosis; payload release in the tumour microenvironment can also support a bystander effect.

title: Perioperative durvalumab with neoadjuvant chemotherapy in operable muscle-invasive bladder cancer
population: 1063 cisplatin-eligible patients with operable muscle-invasive bladder cancer
summary: Perioperative durvalumab with neoadjuvant gemcitabine-cisplatin followed by cystectomy and adjuvant durvalumab improved 24-month event-free survival from 59.8% to 67.8% and overall survival from 75.2% to 82.2%.
criticalReview: NIAGARA is a phase III perioperative immunotherapy trial with dual primary efficacy endpoints and a key controlled OS endpoint. The absolute effects are an 8-point improvement in 24-month EFS (NNT 13) and a 7-point improvement in 24-month OS (NNT 15). Grade 3–4 treatment-related adverse events were similar between groups (40.6% vs 40.9%).

title: Sacituzumab govitecan versus physician's-choice chemotherapy in previously treated metastatic triple-negative breast cancer
journal: Journal of Clinical Oncology; final efficacy analysis
summary: Final analysis: median PFS 4.8 vs 1.7 months (HR 0.41, 95% CI 0.33–0.52); median OS 11.8 vs 6.9 months (HR 0.51, 95% CI 0.42–0.63).

absoluteEffect.absoluteBenefit: Median difference 4.9 months; not an NNT
absoluteEffect.nnt: Not calculated; median OS difference is not a valid NNT
absoluteEffect.toxicity: Grade ≥3 neutropenia about 51%; grade ≥3 diarrhoea about 10%.

clinicalInterpretation: Sacituzumab govitecan improves PFS and OS in previously treated metastatic TNBC. Monitor neutropenia and diarrhoea; median survival differences are not NNTs.
population: 529 randomized; primary efficacy population 468 patients with relapsed/refractory metastatic TNBC, excluding brain metastases.
archiveNote: Full prior Trial-of-the-Day analysis preserved when rotated on 2026-10-21.

title: Cisplatin versus cetuximab with definitive radiotherapy for HPV-positive oropharyngeal cancer
journal: The Lancet; primary randomized phase III publication
summary: Five-year OS was 84.6% with cisplatin versus 77.9% with cetuximab; cetuximab-vs-cisplatin HR 1.45 (95% CI 1.03–2.05), p=0.0163. Cetuximab failed the prespecified non-inferiority criterion.

absoluteEffect.absoluteBenefit: 6.7 percentage points in favour of cisplatin
absoluteEffect.nnt: Approx. 15 at 5 years, based on rounded fixed-time OS rates
absoluteEffect.toxicity: Moderate-to-severe acute/late toxicity not significantly reduced with cetuximab; cisplatin and cetuximab have distinct toxicity profiles.

clinicalInterpretation: In cisplatin-eligible HPV-positive oropharyngeal cancer, cetuximab is not an efficacy-equivalent de-escalation substitute. It failed non-inferiority and showed worse OS.
population: 849 eligible patients with HPV-positive oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma.
archiveNote: Full Trial of the Day record preserved during 22 October rotation.

title: Tremelimumab plus durvalumab versus sorafenib in unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma
population: 1,171 patients randomized among STRIDE, durvalumab monotherapy and sorafenib.
treatment: STRIDE: tremelimumab 300 mg once plus durvalumab 1,500 mg every 4 weeks.
summary: Median OS 16.43 vs 13.77 months; HR 0.78 (96.02% CI 0.65–0.93; p=0.0035). Three-year OS 30.7% vs 20.2%. Grade 3–4 treatment-emergent AEs 50.5% vs 52.4%.

absoluteEffect.nnt: Approx. 10 at 3 years from fixed-time OS rates, not from median survival.
absoluteEffect.nnh: Not calculated without defensible fixed-time excess-harm risk.

clinicalInterpretation: STRIDE showed OS superiority over sorafenib. Durvalumab monotherapy was non-inferior, not superior, for OS; these comparisons must not be conflated. Consider hepatic reserve and immune-mediated hepatitis.
archiveNote: Full Trial-of-the-Day record preserved when rotated on 23 October 2026.

title: Five-year outcomes of perioperative pembrolizumab for resectable early-stage NSCLC
journal: Annals of Oncology; five-year outcomes report (2026)
population: 797 patients with previously untreated resectable stage II, IIIA or IIIB (N2) NSCLC.
treatment: Pembrolizumab 200 mg every 3 weeks for 4 neoadjuvant cycles with platinum-doublet chemotherapy, followed by surgery and up to 13 adjuvant pembrolizumab cycles.
comparator: Placebo plus the same chemotherapy, surgery and adjuvant placebo.

absoluteEffect.nnt: Approx. 5 at 5 years from fixed-time EFS rates; not calculated from the HR.
absoluteEffect.toxicity: Earlier primary analysis reported grade 3–5 treatment-related AEs of 45% vs 38%; the five-year report described safety as consistent with known profiles.

clinicalInterpretation: Five-year results reinforce durable benefit from perioperative pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy in resectable NSCLC. The studied population was fit for platinum-based chemotherapy and surgery; do not extrapolate to unresectable disease or adjuvant-only regimens.
criticalReview: KEYNOTE-671 provides mature five-year evidence for perioperative pembrolizumab plus platinum-doublet chemotherapy in resectable stage II–IIIB(N2) NSCLC. Five-year EFS was 49.9% vs 26.5% and OS 64.6% vs 53.6%. This is a substantial benefit in a selected resectable, platinum-fit population, balanced against added immune-mediated and chemotherapy-related toxicity and the need to complete surgery and adjuvant treatment. Do not extrapolate to unresectable disease or adjuvant-only regimens.
archiveNote: Preserved as the previous Trial of the Day during the 2026-10-26 rotation; full existing analysis retained.
